activities.anchor: Read two versions of the same moment.
activities.caption: bet before you read on — which line convinces
activities.name: cwReaderPredict

config.q: 'The village was poor.' or 'The church clock was right twice a day only by accident.' — which one makes you believe?
choices: The clock — you drew the poverty yourself, and readers believe conclusions they reach alone
The verdict — naming it plainly makes it true
Neither — belief comes from the writer's authority
Both equally — content decides, not delivery
config.why: One hands down a verdict; the other hands over evidence — nothing was added, something was withheld: the conclusion.

activities.anchor: the glint earns the moon, at the moment the moon matters
activities.caption: show or tell? file each move
activities.name: cwTempoSort

config.prompt: Show or tell? File each move:

items.label: compressed summary — 'They were poor for six years'
interior telling that reaches consciousness no external camera can
the reader computes poverty from repetition and hands still in water
at emotional high points, where participation pays most
in the valleys, where speed serves better than evidence

config.why: One chosen gleam buys the whole sky — calibration, not a ban.

activities.anchor: A conversion shows the dial being turned.
activities.caption: the same family, turned — drag the divider
activities.name: cwStewCompare

config.prompt: The same family, written both ways — drag the divider:

before.label: told flatly
before.text: 'The family was poor and the mother was exhausted.'

after.label: written shown
after.text: 'By the third week of the month there was stew again, and no one said so. His mother stood at the sink with her hands in the water a long time after the dishes were done.'

config.why: Nothing is asserted; the reader computes poverty from repetition and exhaustion from hands that stay in the water — and the silence plants shame and tact no told sentence could.

activities.anchor: Vividness is only the entry fee.
activities.caption: true or false — what a detail must do
activities.name: cwVividJudge

statements.s: A detail earns its place by being striking.
statements.why: The professional question is not 'is it striking?' but 'what does it do?' — reveal character, advance the scene, seed a pattern.

statements.s: The cheque-book on the table at a funeral works because it is literal and meaningful at once.
statements.why: Double duty: money and grief in one object.

statements.s: 'It's just a nice touch' is the sound of a sentence being cut in revision.
statements.why: Details that do one job are decoration, and decoration accumulates into murk.

statements.s: Juxtaposition means the writer explains what each image means.
statements.why: Neither image is commentary — the meaning happens between them, in the reader.

activities.anchor: a fantasy city still needs to know what its drains smell like
activities.caption: the noticing drill, in order
activities.name: cwNoticingOrder

config.prompt: The market exercise — put the drill in order:
items: Stand in the scene and give each sense its turn
Record which odour hit first — not 'the market was lively'
Write down what one vendor shouted, in their words
Note the ground's material under your feet
config.why: Noticing is the trainable half — texture does not care whether the world is real, only whether the writer bothered to be there.

activities.anchor: Three of its properties do most of the work.
activities.caption: the sentence's three instruments
activities.name: cwSentenceMatch

config.prompt: The sentence's instruments — pair each with its effect:

pairs.right: sets causality — 'when the letter arrived, she left' implies dependence where 'and' merely reports
sets emphasis — the end of the sentence is its loudest slot
sets tempo — long ones accumulate; short ones stop the room

config.why: 'He came home. The house was wrong.' — the power is the collision of lengths, not either sentence alone.

activities.anchor: Length is a tempo control, not a merit badge
activities.caption: find the faulty line — the tempo argument
activities.name: cwLengthSpot

config.prompt: One line of this workshop's notes is wrong — click it:
lines: An accumulating sentence carries abundance or confusion.
A short one lands a verdict.
Prose made only of the first kind reads as steam.
The change of pace between sizes does work neither size achieves alone.
So polish means stretching every sentence until it impresses.
config.correction: The skill is the change of gear — the short sentence after the long ones does what neither achieves alone.
config.why: 'He came home. The house was wrong.' — neither sentence is the point; the collision is.

activities.anchor: Adverbs are the usual first casualties
activities.caption: the working revision sequence
activities.name: cwReviseOrder

config.prompt: Revision at the right scales, in a working order:
items: Read aloud and mark every stumble
Cut at the scene level before the sentence level — the big cuts are the cheap ones
Check that every detail does double duty
config.why: Revision is re-seeing at the largest scale first; proofreading is the final ten minutes.
